title: Nameoke (Rockaway)
summary: Nameoke names a traditional locality near Rockaway village in old Hempstead town. The name is interpreted as a fishing-place name rather than a phrase meaning water edge.
map_geometry_source: approximate Rockaway village / Far Rockaway area marker; not an exact fishing station or boundary
history_content: Rockaway locality and fishing-place interpretation are brought together here. The source-correction context is handled as a Historic Moment.
translation_content:
Alternate forms and comparisons include Nameaug, Name-auke, and the related fishing-place form Nemaukak. The meaning is given as a fishing place or where fish are taken.

Why Place Names Matter

“Minority place-names have the power to strengthen indigenous languages, cultures and identity.”

— Lars-Erik Edlund, Naming and Narrating Places: Empowering Sami Traditions and Identities through Popular Place-Making Processes (2016), Project overview

Place-name history should show Native people as active and present, not only as names in old documents.
whereintheworld_content: The point is an approximate general marker for the Rockaway village area. It represents a traditional locality, not an exact recorded boundary or fishing station.
